Legs.Citation: ENVELOPE: the embedding negates the swept quaternion's X and Z components (i ↔ -e23, k ↔ -e12). FixedQ4816.MinValue's unary negation is documented to wrap rather than throw (FixedQ4816.cs's operator- remarks) because MinValue's positive magnitude is exactly 2^47, one raw past MaxValue and therefore unrepresentable in FixedQ4816 at all — not a defect of negation, and not something any FixedQ4816 blade coefficient could hold either. A swept X or Z of exactly long.MinValue therefore embeds as itself instead of the +2^47 this sign convention requires, corrupting entry to GeometricProduct: this was the twin's counterexample (left=[0,1,0,0] right=[0,0,-9223372036854775808,0], lane=0, +2^47 vs -2^47). GeometricAlgebraClaims.ExcludeUnembeddableMinValue folds exactly that one raw value on X and Z (both operands) onto MinValue+1, whose negation is exact; Y and W (never negated by this embedding) keep the full raw range including MinValue unchanged

the acceptance boundary of Exponential, in both directions. Eleven in-domain bivectors are accepted, covering all three branches and the zero-generator scalar algebra: circular at (2,0,0) and (0,2,0), hyperbolic at (1,1,0), degenerate at (1,0,1), a mixed rotor at (3,0,0), the zero bivector, and the translator and screw generators at (3,0,1). Nine out-of-domain inputs are refused, and every refusal is an ArgumentException naming the 'bivector' parameter: a nonzero lane of grade zero, one, three or four; a grade-two element carrying an additional scalar or vector lane; and three genuine grade-two elements of (4,0,0) whose squares are not scalar (e12+e34, e13+e24, and an unequally weighted e12+e34)
every accepted value, and the true exponential of the leading refused input
Legs.Against: the versor identity: Reverse negates every grade-two blade, so for a bivector b the reverse of exp(b) is exp(−b) and exp(b)·Reverse(exp(b)) is exactly 1. That is a standard fact about the exponential of a grade-two element, read here off no implementation — it is applied through GeometricProduct and Reverse, which presented.clifford-reverse-anti-automorphism and the planar twins pin on their own
Legs.Citation: ENVELOPE: a MEASURED-PRECISION statement on the accepted side, since the branches round FixedQ4816.Sqrt, SinCos and Exp2. The worst residual over the eleven accepted cases is 4 raw on the scalar lane and 0 on every other, so the 16-raw ceiling is generous; it sits four thousand times below the 63942 raw by which the refused input's branch value misses

Legs.Subject: the refusal of the non-simple bivector is WARRANTED, not over-strict. In (4,0,0) the blades e12 and e34 commute and are disjoint, so exp(e12+e34) is the product exp(e12)·exp(e34) of two IN-DOMAIN exponentials the same law accepts; the claim confirms that product carries a nonzero e1234 lane, which no branch of the scalar-square closed form can produce, and that it meets the versor identity to one raw. Reconstructing what the closed form would have returned for the same input — the circular branch on the square's scalar lane — gives a value that misses the versor identity by 63942 raw, more than two thirds of a unit, so the refused answer was wrong rather than imprecise

over all 35 signatures with at most four generators, two independently created descriptors of the same signature are equal, agree with their == and != operators and with the boxed Equals, refuse equality with a value of another type, and hash to the same value; and the default descriptor — whose null multiplication table is the deliberate encoding of the zero-generator scalar algebra — is equal to Create(0,0,0) in both directions and hashes with it, as its documented behavior across the whole public surface requires
inequality across all 35·34 ordered pairs of distinct signatures, each pair EXHIBITED computing something different rather than merely reported unequal
Legs.Against: the classical fact that distinct Clifford signatures are distinct algebras: either the generator counts differ, so some blade exists in one and lies outside the other — the claim finds that blade and shows the narrower descriptor refuses the operand the wider accepts — or the counts agree and some generator's square differs, and the claim shows the geometric product of that generator with itself disagrees on the scalar lane. The separating operand is derived from the signatures, never read off the equality being tested

Legs.Subject: Multivector value identity beside the descriptor's: two multivectors built from the same sixteen coefficients are equal and share a hash, and perturbing any single blade by one raw unit — all sixteen tried — breaks equality. The digest is an Fnv1aHash fold rather than a per-process-seeded one, so it is the same value on every run and every machine and may be fingerprinted

a descriptor IS its modulus tail: two descriptors built from equal tails are equal, agree with their == and != operators and the boxed Equals, refuse equality with another type, and share a hash; five tails differing in a coefficient, in a sign, or in degree are each unequal to it; two default descriptors are equal and no constructed one is equal to a default. Over the FixedQ4816 carrier — whose degree-2 surface runs the delegating quadratic lane rather than the general one — the same holds, so the rule is the type's rather than BigInteger's

an Element or a Projective IS its coordinate vector, and the modulus is DELIBERATELY no part of it — the value-level face of the receiver-affinity contract, under which any degree-2 receiver reinterprets a degree-2 vector as its own. The claim pins the choice in both directions at once: One under the tail [1,1] equals One under the tail [5,7], while the two descriptors that produced them stay unequal, so the modulus is distinguished exactly where it is stored and nowhere else. Degree is still part of identity — a degree-2 One is unequal to a degree-1 and a degree-3 One — as are default values, which equal only other defaults

the algebraic identities hold as VALUE equality, through the framework's own comparers rather than only coordinate by coordinate: Add(One, Zero) equals One, Zero equals the all-zero coordinate vector, Root equals MultiplyByRoot(One), a FixedQ4816 element times One lands back on an equal element, ProjectiveStep of two equal windows agrees while a window is unequal to its own successor, and a HashSet holding One both recognizes Add(One, Zero) as the same value and refuses a second read of One as a new one. Elements differing by one raw unit or one coordinate stay unequal. The digest is an Fnv1aHash fold over the carrier's own hash codes rather than a per-process-seeded one, so it is stable across runs and machines
